subject: Cloud Computing
title: Water Usage in Data Centers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Water Usage in Data Centers.

hook.text: A large data center can use 5 million gallons of water per day for cooling. In drought-prone areas, that's a crisis.

buildup.text: Evaporative cooling is efficient but water-intensive. As data centers grow, water scarcity becomes a real concern.

discovery.text: Google and Microsoft now report WUE (Water Usage Effectiveness) alongside PUE. Transparency drives improvement.

twist.text: Some regions are pushing back. Local communities have blocked data center construction over water concerns.

climax.text: Water-free cooling, recycled water systems, and smarter location choices are making data centers less thirsty.

punchline.text: Five million gallons daily. Data centers are learning to drink less.

quiz.question: What is WUE in the context of data centers?
options: Water Usage Effectiveness — a metric for how much water a data center consumes
Workload Utilization Efficiency — a measure of computing power
Wireless Uplink Estimation — a network performance metric

details.summary: Data centers consume billions of gallons of water annually for cooling, particularly evaporative cooling systems common in hot climates. Google and Microsoft have disclosed water usage figures, sparking debate about data center placement in water-stressed regions.
details.whyItMatters: Water consumption is an often-overlooked environmental cost of cloud computing. As data centers expand, competition for water with agriculture and communities becomes a sustainability concern.
takeaways: Evaporative cooling is the largest source of data center water use
Google uses roughly 5 billion gallons of water annually
Data center placement in arid regions raises sustainability concerns

faq.question: Why do data centers use so much water?
faq.answer: Evaporative cooling uses water to absorb heat efficiently, consuming water as it evaporates. A single large data center can use millions of gallons daily. In hot climates where air cooling is insufficient, water-based cooling becomes the primary method for maintaining safe operating temperatures.

faq.question: What alternatives to water cooling exist?
faq.answer: Liquid cooling systems recirculate coolant without evaporation. Locating data centers in cold climates enables free air cooling. Immersion cooling submerges servers in non-conductive liquid. Some facilities use seawater or recycled water to reduce freshwater consumption.
